{"parentUuid":"2c1ba72a-0f21-499d-b4a8-2337238f0b2d","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_co85sz51b427q8jbaabdfqp8","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp3/b/src/format.rs","content":"//! On-disk format.\n//!\n//! The data directory contains three kinds of append-only binary files:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! <root>/\n//!   LOCK                  advisory lock (held while the process is open)\n//!   seg-0000000000000001  committed transaction at version 1 (a \"segment\")\n//!   seg-0000000000000002  committed transaction at version 2\n//!   base-0000000000000005 compacted snapshot of every key at version 5\n//! ```\n//!\n//! * A **segment** `seg-V` is created by transaction commit at version `V`.\n//!   It contains one [`Record::Begin`], zero or more `Put`/`Delete` cells,\n//!   in key order, and one [`Record::Commit`].\n//! * A **base** `base-V` is created by GC/compaction. It contains one\n//!   [`Record::Base`] header followed by one [`Record::Put`] or\n//!   [`Record::Delete`] per key that existed at version `V` (the compaction\n//!   horizon), in key order. It makes every old segment with version\n//!   `<= V` redundant.\n//!\n//! Both files are written through `Vfs::write_atomic`: temp file → fsync →\n//! atomic rename → fsync directory. Recovery therefore only ever observes\n//! whole files; a CRC is still checked on every frame to catch torn or\n//! corrupt bytes.\n//!\n//! Frame layout (all integers little-endian):\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! u32 magic   = 0x4D56_4343 (\"MVCC\")\n//! u8  record  = 1 Begin | 2 Commit | 3 Base | 4 Put | 5 Delete\n//! u32 length  = payload byte length\n//! [payload]\n//! u32 crc32   = CRC32 over magic..payload (IEEE 802.3 polynomial)\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Payloads:\n//! * Begin  / Commit: `u64 version`\n//! * Base:            `u64 horizon_version`\n//! * Put / Delete:    `u32 key_len | key bytes | u64 cell_version`\n//!                    (Put additionally: `u32 val_len | value bytes`)\n\nuse std::io::{Cursor, Read, Write};\nuse std::path::Path;\n\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::vfs::SharedVfs;\n\npub const MAGIC: u32 = 0x4D56_4343;\n\npub const REC_BEGIN: u8 = 1;\npub const REC_COMMIT: u8 = 2;\npub const REC_BASE: u8 = 3;\npub const REC_PUT: u8 = 4;\npub const REC_DELETE: u8 = 5;\n\n/// One decoded cell version.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Cell {\n    pub key: Vec<u8>,\n    pub val: Option<Vec<u8>>,\n    /// Version under which this value/tombstone was committed.\n    pub version: u64,\n}\n\n/// A file replayed from disk.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Segment {\n    /// Version of this file: transaction version for segments, horizon\n    /// version for bases.\n    pub version: u64,\n    pub is_base: bool,\n    pub cells: Vec<Cell>,\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// CRC32 (IEEE, same polynomial as zlib/gzip)\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nconst CRC_POLY: u32 = 0xEDB8_8320;\n\nconst fn crc_table() -> [u32; 256] {\n    let mut table = [0u32; 256];\n    let mut i = 0usize;\n    while i < 256 {\n        let mut c = i as u32;\n        let mut k = 0;\n        while k < 8 {\n            c = if c & 1 != 0 {\n                CRC_POLY ^ (c >> 1)\n            } else {\n                c >> 1\n            };\n            k += 1;\n        }\n        table[i] = c;\n        i += 1;\n    }\n    table\n}\n\nstatic CRC_TABLE: [u32; 256] = crc_table();\n\npub fn crc32(data: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n    let mut c = 0xFFFF_FFFFu32;\n    for &b in data {\n        c = CRC_TABLE[((c ^ b as u32) & 0xFF) as usize] ^ (c >> 8);\n    }\n    c ^ 0xFFFF_FFFF\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Encoding\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nstruct Frame {\n    kind: u8,\n    payload: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\nfn encode_frame(kind: u8, payload: Vec<u8>) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(13 + payload.len());\n    out.extend_from_slice(&MAGIC.to_le_bytes());\n    out.push(kind);\n    out.extend_from_slice(&(payload.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n    out.extend_from_slice(&payload);\n    let crc = crc32(&out);\n    out.extend_from_slice(&crc.to_le_bytes());\n    out\n}\n\nfn put_u64(buf: &mut Vec<u8>, v: u64) {\n    buf.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());\n}\n\nfn put_cell_payload(cell: &Cell, kind: u8) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let mut p = Vec::new();\n    p.extend_from_slice(&(cell.key.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n    p.extend_from_slice(&cell.key);\n    put_u64(&mut p, cell.version);\n    if kind == REC_PUT {\n        let val = cell.val.as_ref().expect(\"put cell must carry a value\");\n        p.extend_from_slice(&(val.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n        p.extend_from_slice(val);\n    }\n    p\n}\n\n/// Serialize a committed transaction (segment file body).\n/// Cells are sorted by key for deterministic files.\npub fn encode_segment(version: u64, cells: &mut [Cell]) -> Vec<u8> {\n    cells.sort_by(|a, b| a.key.cmp(&b.key));\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\n    let mut hdr = Vec::new();\n    put_u64(&mut hdr, version);\n    out.extend_from_slice(&encode_frame(REC_BEGIN, hdr));\n    for c in cells.iter() {\n        let kind = if c.val.is_some() { REC_PUT } else { REC_DELETE };\n        out.extend_from_slice(&encode_frame(kind, put_cell_payload(c, kind)));\n    }\n    let mut ftr = Vec::new();\n    put_u64(&mut ftr, version);\n    out.extend_from_slice(&encode_frame(REC_COMMIT, ftr));\n    out\n}\n\n/// Serialize a compacted base file body.\npub fn encode_base(horizon: u64, cells: &mut [Cell]) -> Vec<u8> {\n    cells.sort_by(|a, b| a.key.cmp(&b.key));\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\n    let mut hdr = Vec::new();\n    put_u64(&mut hdr, horizon);\n    out.extend_from_slice(&encode_frame(REC_BASE, hdr));\n    for c in cells.iter() {\n        let kind = if c.val.is_some() { REC_PUT } else { REC_DELETE };\n        out.extend_from_slice(&encode_frame(kind, put_cell_payload(c, kind)));\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Decoding\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nfn read_exact_opt(data: &[u8], pos: &mut usize, n: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {\n    if *pos + n > data.len() {\n        return Err(Error::corrupt(format!(\n            \"unexpected end of file at byte {} (need {})\",\n            pos, n\n        )));\n    }\n    let out = data[*pos..*pos + n].to_vec();\n    *pos += n;\n    Ok(out)\n}\n\nfn read_u32(data: &[u8], pos: &mut usize) -> Result<u32> {\n    let b = read_exact_opt(data, pos, 4)?;\n    Ok(u32::from_le_bytes([b[0], b[1], b[2], b[3]]))\n}\n\nfn read_u64(data: &[u8], pos: &mut usize) -> Result<u64> {\n    let b = read_exact_opt(data, pos, 8)?;\n    Ok(u64::from_le_bytes([\n        b[0], b[1], b[2], b[3], b[4], b[5], b[6], b[7],\n    ]))\n}\n\nfn decode_cell(kind: u8, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<Cell> {\n    let mut pos = 0;\n    let key_len = read_u32(payload, &mut pos)? as usize;\n    let key = read_exact_opt(payload, &mut pos, key_len)?;\n    let version = read_u64(payload, &mut pos)?;\n    let val = if kind == REC_PUT {\n        let val_len = read_u32(payload, &mut pos)? as usize;\n        let v = read_exact_opt(payload, &mut pos, val_len)?;\n        if pos != payload.len() {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(\"put cell has trailing bytes\"));\n        }\n        Some(v)\n    } else {\n        if pos != payload.len() {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(\"delete cell has trailing bytes\"));\n        }\n        None\n    };\n    Ok(Cell { key, val, version })\n}\n\n/// Parse one segment/base file body.\npub fn decode_file(name: &str, data: &[u8]) -> Result<Segment> {\n    let mut pos = 0;\n    let mut cells = Vec::new();\n    let mut begin_version = None;\n    let mut commit_version = None;\n    let mut is_base = false;\n\n    while pos < data.len() {\n        let frame_start = pos;\n        let magic = read_u32(data, &mut pos)?;\n        if magic != MAGIC {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(format!(\n                \"{name}: bad magic at byte {frame_start}\"\n            )));\n        }\n        let kind = *read_exact_opt(data, &mut pos, 1)?\n            .first()\n            .ok_or_else(|| Error::corrupt(\"missing record kind\"))?;\n        let len = read_u32(data, &mut pos)? as usize;\n        let payload = read_exact_opt(data, &mut pos, len)?;\n        let want_crc = read_u32(data, &mut pos)?;\n        let header_and_payload = &data[frame_start..frame_start + 9 + len];\n        if crc32(header_and_payload) != want_crc {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(format!(\n                \"{name}: crc mismatch at byte {frame_start}\"\n            )));\n        }\n\n        let mut p = Cursor::new(&payload);\n        match kind {\n            REC_BEGIN => {\n                let mut b = [0u8; 8];\n                p.read_exact(&mut b)?;\n                begin_version = Some(u64::from_le_bytes(b));\n            }\n            REC_COMMIT => {\n                let mut b = [0u8; 8];\n                p.read_exact(&mut b)?;\n                commit_version = Some(u64::from_le_bytes(b));\n            }\n            REC_BASE => {\n                let mut b = [0u8; 8];\n                p.read_exact(&mut b)?;\n                begin_version = Some(u64::from_le_bytes(b));\n                is_base = true;\n            }\n            REC_PUT | REC_DELETE => {\n                cells.push(decode_cell(kind, &payload)?);\n            }\n            other => {\n                return Err(Error::corrupt(format!(\n                    \"{name}: unknown record kind {other}\"\n                )))\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    let version = begin_version.ok_or_else(|| {\n        Error::corrupt(format!(\"{name}: missing begin/base header\"))\n    })?;\n    if !is_base {\n        match commit_version {\n            Some(cv) if cv == version => {}\n            Some(cv) => {\n                return Err(Error::corrupt(format!(\n                    \"{name}: begin version {version} != commit version {cv}\"\n                )))\n            }\n            None => return Err(Error::corrupt(format!(\"{name}: missing commit\"))),\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(Segment {\n        version,\n        is_base,\n        cells,\n    })\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// File naming\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\npub fn segment_name(version: u64) -> String {\n    format!(\"seg-{version:016x}\")\n}\n\npub fn base_name(version: u64) -> String {\n    format!(\"base-{version:016x}\")\n}\n\npub fn parse_versioned_name(name: &str) -> Option<(u64, bool)> {\n    let (prefix, is_base) = if let Some(v) = name.strip_prefix(\"seg-\") {\n        (v, false)\n    } else if let Some(v) = name.strip_prefix(\"base-\") {\n        (v, true)\n    } else {\n        return None;\n    };\n    let version = u64::from_str_radix(prefix, 16).ok()?;\n    Some((version, is_base))\n}\n\npub fn is_temp_name(name: &str) -> bool {\n    name.starts_with('.') && name.ends_with(\".tmp\")\n}\n\n/// Read an entire small file through the VFS.\npub fn read_whole(vfs: &SharedVfs, path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {\n    let mut f = vfs.open_read(path)?;\n    let mut buf = Vec::new();\n    f.read_to_end(&mut buf)?;\n    Ok(buf)\n}\n\n/// Helper kept for symmetry / tests: round-trip bytes through a writer.\npub fn write_vec(w: &mut Vec<u8>, bytes: &[u8]) {\n    w.write_all(bytes).expect(\"vec write cannot fail\");\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_80370685314a708ad0335a7b","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":1016,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":43832,"output_tokens":3546,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_co85sz51b427q8jbaabdfqp8":{"content":"//! {"parentUuid":"1d6de14d-21a4-4b2d-9191-5de24a6f35ec","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_0nqm1x5tgno9pd17iq622tly","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp3/b/src/engine.rs","content":"//! Snapshot-isolation MVCC engine with snapshot-aware version reclamation.\n//!\n//! ## Concurrency model\n//!\n//! The store is single-process. A single `Mutex` serializes the *state*\n//! transitions; the only slow operation performed while holding it is the\n//! final `fsync` of a commit (commit is a critical section by design:\n//! versions are allocated in commit order). Reads from long-lived snapshots\n//! do not take the lock across I/O — they resolve an in-memory version\n//! index, while the bytes for every version they may see are protected from\n//! reclamation by the snapshot's pin (see [`Engine::gc`]).\n//!\n//! ## Versions\n//!\n//! Every successful commit allocates the next monotonic `u64` version.\n//! Transactions and explicit snapshots read at the version that was current\n//! when they started.\n//!\n//! ## Reclamation invariant\n//!\n//! `gc()` compacts to a *horizon* `H` = the minimum read version of every\n//! active transaction and explicit snapshot (or the latest committed\n//! version when nothing is active). It writes one base file containing the\n//! visible value of every key at `H`, and only then deletes files whose\n//! version is `<= H`. Because no active reader reads at a version below\n//! `H`, no version still needed is ever deleted; conversely, when a long\n//! reader pins an old version, old segments are retained until the pin is\n//! released.\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\n\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::format::{self, Cell, Segment};\nuse crate::vfs::{FaultVfs, SharedVfs};\n\n/// One committed version of one key (value `None` = delete tombstone).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\nstruct Entry {\n    version: u64,\n    val: Option<Vec<u8>>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct FileMeta {\n    is_base: bool,\n    size: u64,\n    /// True once GC has logically replaced this file but the unlink failed.\n    stale: bool,\n}\n\n/// An open read-write transaction.\nstruct TxState {\n    read_version: u64,\n    writes: BTreeMap<Vec<u8>, Option<Vec<u8>>>,\n}\n\n/// An explicit long-lived read snapshot pin.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct SnapshotInfo {\n    pub id: u64,\n    pub version: u64,\n}\n\n/// Result of a compaction pass.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct GcReport {\n    pub horizon: u64,\n    pub base_version_before: u64,\n    pub base_written: bool,\n    pub base_cells: usize,\n    pub files_removed: usize,\n    pub bytes_reclaimed: u64,\n    /// Obsolete files whose unlink failed; they will be retried on the next\n    /// pass or at reopen.\n    pub stale_left: usize,\n    pub noop_reason: Option<&'static str>,\n}\n\n/// Engine statistics, also serialized by the HTTP layer.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Stats {\n    pub current_version: u64,\n    pub base_version: u64,\n    pub keys: usize,\n    pub live_cells: usize,\n    pub open_transactions: Vec<(u64, u64)>,\n    pub snapshots: Vec<SnapshotInfo>,\n    pub segment_files: usize,\n    pub base_files: usize,\n    pub stale_files: usize,\n    pub live_bytes: u64,\n    pub stale_bytes: u64,\n}\n\nstruct Inner {\n    root: PathBuf,\n    vfs: SharedVfs,\n    /// Next version to allocate (current committed version = `next_version - 1`).\n    next_version: u64,\n    /// Horizon of the newest compacted base (0 = no base yet).\n    base_version: u64,\n    index: BTreeMap<Vec<u8>, Vec<Entry>>,\n    txs: BTreeMap<u64, TxState>,\n    snapshots: BTreeMap<u64, SnapshotInfo>,\n    /// Every file known on disk, keyed by its version.\n    files: BTreeMap<u64, FileMeta>,\n    next_tx_id: u64,\n    next_snap_id: u64,\n}\n\n/// Handle to an open store. Cheap to clone (`Arc` inside).\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct Engine {\n    inner: Arc<Mutex<Inner>>,\n    faults: FaultVfs,\n}\n\nimpl Engine {\n    /// Open (or create) a store in `root` on the given file system.\n    ///\n    /// A `LOCK` file in `root` prevents two engines on the same directory\n    /// at once (single-node process boundary).\n    pub fn open(root: impl Into<PathBuf>, vfs: SharedVfs) -> Result<Engine> {\n        Self::open_faulted(root, FaultVfs::new(vfs))\n    }\n\n    /// Open with an externally constructed [`FaultVfs`], so callers can arm\n    /// I/O faults around open/GC as well as commits.\n    pub fn open_faulted(root: impl Into<PathBuf>, faults: FaultVfs) -> Result<Engine> {\n        let root = root.into();\n        let vfs: SharedVfs = Arc::new(faults.clone());\n        vfs.create_dir_all(&root)?;\n\n        let lock = root.join(\"LOCK\");\n        if vfs.exists(&lock) {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(\n                \"LOCK present: another engine has this directory open\",\n            ));\n        }\n        vfs.write_atomic(&lock, b\"mvcc-gc lock\")?;\n\n        // Clean crash debris from interrupted publications.\n        for e in vfs.list_dir(&root)? {\n            if format::is_temp_name(&e.name) {\n                let _ = vfs.remove_file(&root.join(&e.name));\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Discover data files.\n        let mut on_disk: BTreeMap<u64, FileMeta> = BTreeMap::new();\n        let mut newest_base = 0u64;\n        for e in vfs.list_dir(&root)? {\n            if !e.is_file {\n                continue;\n            }\n            if let Some((version, is_base)) = format::parse_versioned_name(&e.name) {\n                let data = format::read_whole(&vfs, &root.join(&e.name))?;\n                let _seg: Segment = format::decode_file(&e.name, &data)?;\n                if is_base {\n                    newest_base = newest_base.max(version);\n                }\n                on_disk.insert(\n                    version,\n                    FileMeta {\n                        is_base,\n                        size: data.len() as u64,\n                        stale: false,\n                    },\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Interrupted GC may have left files the new base obsoletes.\n        for (&v, meta) in &on_disk {\n            if v <= newest_base && !(meta.is_base && v == newest_base) {\n                let name = if meta.is_base {\n                    format::base_name(v)\n                } else {\n                    format::segment_name(v)\n                };\n                let _ = vfs.remove_file(&root.join(name));\n            }\n        }\n        on_disk.retain(|v, m| *v > newest_base || (m.is_base && *v == newest_base));\n\n        // Replay: base first, then surviving segments in version order.\n        let mut index: BTreeMap<Vec<u8>, Vec<Entry>> = BTreeMap::new();\n        let mut next_version = 1u64;\n        for (&v, meta) in &on_disk {\n            next_version = next_version.max(v + 1);\n            let name = if meta.is_base {\n                format::base_name(v)\n            } else {\n                format::segment_name(v)\n            };\n            let data = format::read_whole(&vfs, &root.join(&name))?;\n            let seg = format::decode_file(&name, &data)?;\n            for c in seg.cells {\n                apply_cell(\n                    &mut index,\n                    Entry {\n                        version: c.version,\n                        val: c.val,\n                    },\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(Engine {\n            inner: Arc::new(Mutex::new(Inner {\n                root,\n                vfs,\n                next_version,\n                base_version: newest_base,\n                index,\n                txs: BTreeMap::new(),\n                snapshots: BTreeMap::new(),\n                files: on_disk,\n                next_tx_id: 1,\n                next_snap_id: 1,\n            })),\n            faults,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Fault-injection handle (no-op unless faults are armed).\n    pub fn faults(&self) -> &FaultVfs {\n        &self.faults\n    }\n\n    /// Begin a transaction; returns `(tx_id, read_version)`.\n    pub fn begin(&self) -> (u64, u64) {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let id = g.next_tx_id;\n        g.next_tx_id += 1;\n        let read_version = g.next_version - 1;\n        g.txs.insert(\n            id,\n            TxState {\n                read_version,\n                writes: BTreeMap::new(),\n            },\n        );\n        (id, read_version)\n    }\n\n    /// Pin an explicit long-lived read snapshot at the current version.\n    pub fn snapshot(&self) -> SnapshotInfo {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let id = g.next_snap_id;\n        g.next_snap_id += 1;\n        let info = SnapshotInfo {\n            id,\n            version: g.next_version - 1,\n        };\n        g.snapshots.insert(id, info.clone());\n        info\n    }\n\n    pub fn release_snapshot(&self, id: u64) -> Result<()> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        match g.snapshots.remove(&id) {\n            Some(_) => Ok(()),\n            None => Err(Error::UnknownSnapshot(id)),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn put(&self, tx: u64, key: Vec<u8>, val: Vec<u8>) -> Result<()> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        g.tx_mut(tx)?.writes.insert(key, Some(val));\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub fn delete(&self, tx: u64, key: Vec<u8>) -> Result<()> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        g.tx_mut(tx)?.writes.insert(key, None);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Read inside a transaction: own buffered writes win, otherwise the\n    /// newest committed version `<=` its read snapshot.\n    pub fn get_tx(&self, tx: u64, key: &[u8]) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>> {\n        let g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let t = g.txs.get(&tx).ok_or(Error::UnknownTx(tx))?;\n        if let Some(v) = t.writes.get(key) {\n            return Ok(v.clone());\n        }\n        Ok(read_at(&g.index, key, t.read_version))\n    }\n\n    /// Read through an explicit snapshot pin.\n    pub fn get_snapshot(&self, snap: u64, key: &[u8]) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>> {\n        let g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let s = g.snapshots.get(&snap).ok_or(Error::UnknownSnapshot(snap))?;\n        Ok(read_at(&g.index, key, s.version))\n    }\n\n    /// Abort/discard a transaction.\n    pub fn abort(&self, tx: u64) -> Result<()> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        match g.txs.remove(&tx) {\n            Some(_) => Ok(()),\n            None => Err(Error::UnknownTx(tx)),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Commit: first-writer-wins conflict check, then durable publication\n    /// at the next monotonic version.\n    ///\n    /// On I/O failure nothing is published and the transaction stays open\n    /// (the caller may retry the commit or abort).\n    pub fn commit(&self, tx: u64) -> Result<u64> {\n        // Phase 1: conflict check under the lock and stage the payload.\n        let (version, mut cells, file_size_hint) = {\n            let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n            let t = g.txs.get(&tx).ok_or(Error::UnknownTx(tx))?;\n            let read_version = t.read_version;\n            for key in t.writes.keys() {\n                if let Some(entry) = g.index.get(key).and_then(|v| v.last()) {\n                    if entry.version > read_version {\n                        return Err(Error::Conflict(key.clone()));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            let version = g.next_version;\n            let mut cells: Vec<Cell> = t\n                .writes\n                .iter()\n                .map(|(k, v)| Cell {\n                    key: k.clone(),\n                    val: v.clone(),\n                    version,\n                })\n                .collect();\n            let body = format::encode_segment(version, &mut cells);\n            (version, cells, body.len() as u64)\n        };\n\n        // Phase 2: durable publication (temp -> fsync -> rename -> fsync dir).\n        let name = format::segment_name(version);\n        let path = self.inner.lock().unwrap().root.join(name);\n        let body = {\n            let g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n            let mut cells2: Vec<Cell> = cells\n                .iter()\n                .map(|c| Cell {\n                    key: c.key.clone(),\n                    val: c.val.clone(),\n                    version,\n                })\n                .collect();\n            // Re-encode outside borrow games; cells already sorted.\n            let _ = &g;\n            format::encode_segment(version, &mut cells2)\n        };\n        // Publish through the VFS. Any error leaves no file behind.\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().vfs.write_atomic(&path, &body)?;\n\n        // Phase 3: publish into the in-memory index atomically with version.\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        // Another commit on the same engine cannot race (mutex), but defend\n        // the invariant explicitly.\n        assert_eq!(g.next_version, version, \"version allocated out of order\");\n        for c in cells.drain(..) {\n            apply_cell(\n                &mut g.index,\n                Entry {\n                    version,\n                    val: c.val,\n                },\n            );\n        }\n        g.files.insert(\n            version,\n            FileMeta {\n                is_base: false,\n                size: file_size_hint,\n                stale: false,\n            },\n        );\n        g.next_version = version + 1;\n        g.txs.remove(&tx);\n        Ok(version)\n    }\n\n    /// Current committed version.\n    pub fn current_version(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().next_version - 1\n    }\n\n    /// Snapshot pins, oldest first.\n    pub fn list_snapshots(&self) -> Vec<SnapshotInfo> {\n        let g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        g.snapshots.values().cloned().collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Compaction horizon: min read version over all active txs/snapshots.\n    fn horizon(g: &Inner) -> u64 {\n        let latest = g.next_version - 1;\n        let mut h = latest;\n        for t in g.txs.values() {\n            h = h.min(t.read_version);\n        }\n        for s in g.snapshots.values() {\n            h = h.min(s.version);\n        }\n        h\n    }\n\n    /// Run one reclamation pass. See module docs for the invariant.\n    pub fn gc(&self) -> Result<GcReport> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n\n        let horizon = Self::horizon(&g);\n        let mut report = GcReport {\n            horizon,\n            base_version_before: g.base_version,\n            base_written: false,\n            base_cells: 0,\n            files_removed: 0,\n            bytes_reclaimed: 0,\n            stale_left: 0,\n            noop_reason: None,\n        };\n\n        if horizon <= g.base_version {\n            report.noop_reason = Some(\"horizon already covered by newest base\");\n            report.stale_left = g.files.values().filter(|m| m.stale).count();\n            return Ok(report);\n        }\n\n        // Build the base: for every key, its newest entry visible at H.\n        // Tombstones are dropped — the files containing the key's older\n        // versions are all removed with this pass, so absence is identical\n        // to a tombstone for every snapshot that can still be read.\n        let mut base_cells: Vec<Cell> = Vec::new();\n        let mut prune: Vec<(Vec<u8>, Entry)> = Vec::new();\n        for (key, entries) in &g.index {\n            let mut keep: Option<&Entry> = None;\n            for e in entries {\n                if e.version <= horizon {\n                    keep = Some(e);\n                } else {\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n            if let Some(e) = keep {\n                if e.val.is_some() {\n                    base_cells.push(Cell {\n                        key: key.clone(),\n                        val: e.val.clone(),\n                        version: e.version,\n                    });\n                }\n                prune.push((key.clone(), e.clone()));\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Publish the base before deleting anything.\n        let body = format::encode_base(horizon, &mut base_cells);\n        let base_path = g.root.join(format::base_name(horizon));\n        let base_size = body.len() as u64;\n        g.vfs.write_atomic(&base_path, &body)?;\n\n        // Now mark every file <= H obsolete and unlink it. A failed unlink\n        // leaves a harmless stale file retried later; the base already\n        // supersedes it, so this never blocks future commits.\n        let obsolete: Vec<(u64, FileMeta)> = g\n            .files\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|(v, _)| **v <= horizon)\n            .map(|(v, m)| (*v, m.clone()))\n            .collect();\n\n        for (v, meta) in obsolete {\n            let name = if meta.is_base {\n                format::base_name(v)\n            } else {\n                format::segment_name(v)\n            };\n            match g.vfs.remove_file(&g.root.join(name)) {\n                Ok(()) => {\n                    g.files.remove(&v);\n                    report.files_removed += 1;\n                    report.bytes_reclaimed += meta.size;\n                }\n                Err(_) => {\n                    if let Some(m) = g.files.get_mut(&v) {\n                        m.stale = true;\n                    }\n                    report.stale_left += 1;\n                    report.bytes_reclaimed += 0;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        g.files.insert(\n            horizon,\n            FileMeta {\n                is_base: true,\n                size: base_size,\n                stale: false,\n            },\n        );\n        g.base_version = horizon;\n\n        // Prune in-memory history: all readers that remain read at >= H, so\n        // only the newest entry <= H per key must survive alongside entries\n        // newer than H.\n        for (key, keep) in prune {\n            if let Some(entries) = g.index.get_mut(&key) {\n                entries.retain(|e| e.version > horizon);\n                entries.insert(0, keep);\n            }\n        }\n\n        report.base_written = true;\n        report.base_cells = base_cells.len();\n        Ok(report)\n    }\n\n    /// Snapshot of counters for observability/tests.\n    pub fn stats(&self) -> Stats {\n Because no active reader reads at a version below\n//! `H`, no version still needed is ever deleted; conversely, when a long\n//! reader pins an old version, old segments are retained until the pin is\n//! released.\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\n\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::format::{self, Cell, Segment};\nuse crate::vfs::{FaultVfs, SharedVfs};\n\n/// One committed version of one key (value `None` = delete tombstone).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\nstruct Entry {\n    version: u64,\n    val: Option<Vec<u8>>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct FileMeta {\n    is_base: bool,\n    size: u64,\n    /// True once GC has logically replaced this file but the unlink failed.\n    stale: bool,\n}\n\n/// An open read-write transaction.\nstruct TxState {\n    read_version: u64,\n    writes: BTreeMap<Vec<u8>, Option<Vec<u8>>>,\n}\n\n/// An explicit long-lived read snapshot pin.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct SnapshotInfo {\n    pub id: u64,\n    pub version: u64,\n}\n\n/// Result of a compaction pass.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct GcReport {\n    pub horizon: u64,\n    pub base_version_before: u64,\n    pub base_written: bool,\n    pub base_cells: usize,\n    pub files_removed: usize,\n    pub bytes_reclaimed: u64,\n    /// Obsolete files whose unlink failed; A single `Mutex` serializes the *state*\n//! transitions; the only slow operation performed while holding it is the\n//! final `fsync` of a commit (commit is a critical section by design:\n//! versions are allocated in commit order). Reads from long-lived snapshots\n//! do not take the lock across I/O — they resolve an in-memory version\n//! index, while the bytes for every version they may see are protected from\n//! reclamation by the snapshot's pin (see [`Engine::gc`]).\n//!\n//! ## Versions\n//!\n//! Every successful commit allocates the next monotonic `u64` version.\n//! Transactions and explicit snapshots read at the version that was current\n//! when they started.\n//!\n//! ## Reclamation invariant\n//!\n//! `gc()` compacts to a *horizon* `H` = the minimum read version of every\n//! active transaction and explicit snapshot (or the latest committed\n//! version when nothing is active). It writes one base file containing the\n//! visible value of every key at `H`, and only then deletes files whose\n//! version is `<= H`. Because no active reader reads at a version below\n//! `H`, no version still needed is ever deleted; conversely, when a long\n//! reader pins an old version, old segments are retained until the pin is\n//! released.\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\n\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::format::{self, Cell, Segment};\nuse crate::vfs::{FaultVfs, SharedVfs};\n\n/// One committed version of one key (value `None` = delete tombstone).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\nstruct Entry {\n    version: u64,\n    val: Option<Vec<u8>>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct FileMeta {\n    is_base: bool,\n    size: u64,\n    /// True once GC has logically replaced this file but the unlink failed.\n    stale: bool,\n}\n\n/// An open read-write transaction.\nstruct TxState {\n    read_version: u64,\n    writes: BTreeMap<Vec<u8>, Option<Vec<u8>>>,\n}\n\n/// An explicit long-lived read snapshot pin.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct SnapshotInfo {\n    pub id: u64,\n    pub version: u64,\n}\n\n/// Result of a compaction pass.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct GcReport {\n    pub horizon: u64,\n    pub base_version_before: u64,\n    pub base_written: bool,\n    pub base_cells: usize,\n    pub files_removed: usize,\n    pub bytes_reclaimed: u64,\n    /// Obsolete files whose unlink failed; they will be retried on the next\n    /// pass or at reopen.\n    pub stale_left: usize,\n    pub noop_reason: Option<&'static str>,\n}\n\n/// Engine statistics, also serialized by the HTTP layer.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Stats {\n    pub current_version: u64,\n    pub base_version: u64,\n    pub keys: usize,\n    pub live_cells: usize,\n    pub open_transactions: Vec<(u64, u64)>,\n    pub snapshots: Vec<SnapshotInfo>,\n    pub segment_files: usize,\n    pub base_files: usize,\n    pub stale_files: usize,\n    pub live_bytes: u64,\n    pub stale_bytes: u64,\n}\n\nstruct Inner {\n    root: PathBuf,\n    vfs: SharedVfs,\n    /// Next version to allocate (current committed version = `next_version - 1`).\n    next_version: u64,\n    /// Horizon of the newest compacted base (0 = no base yet).\n    base_version: u64,\n    index: BTreeMap<Vec<u8>, Vec<Entry>>,\n    txs: BTreeMap<u64, TxState>,\n    snapshots: BTreeMap<u64, SnapshotInfo>,\n    /// Every file known on disk, keyed by its version.\n    files: BTreeMap<u64, FileMeta>,\n    next_tx_id: u64,\n    next_snap_id: u64,\n}\n\n/// Handle to an open store. Cheap to clone (`Arc` inside).\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct Engine {\n    inner: Arc<Mutex<Inner>>,\n    faults: FaultVfs,\n}\n\nimpl Engine {\n    /// Open (or create) a store in `root` on the given file system.\n    ///\n    /// A `LOCK` file in `root` prevents two engines on the same directory\n    /// at once (single-node process boundary).\n    pub fn open(root: impl Into<PathBuf>, vfs: SharedVfs) -> Result<Engine> {\n        Self::open_faulted(root, FaultVfs::new(vfs))\n    }\n\n    /// Open with an externally constructed [`FaultVfs`], so callers can arm\n    /// I/O faults around open/GC as well as commits.\n    pub fn open_faulted(root: impl Into<PathBuf>, faults: FaultVfs) -> Result<Engine> {\n        let root = root.into();\n        let vfs: SharedVfs = Arc::new(faults.clone());\n        vfs.create_dir_all(&root)?;\n\n        let lock = root.join(\"LOCK\");\n        if vfs.exists(&lock) {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(\n                \"LOCK present: another engine has this directory open\",\n            ));\n        }\n        vfs.write_atomic(&lock, b\"mvcc-gc lock\")?;\n\n        // Clean crash debris from interrupted publications.\n        for e in vfs.list_dir(&root)? {\n            if format::is_temp_name(&e.name) {\n                let _ = vfs.remove_file(&root.join(&e.name));\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Discover data files.\n        let mut on_disk: BTreeMap<u64, FileMeta> = BTreeMap::new();\n        let mut newest_base = 0u64;\n        for e in vfs.list_dir(&root)? {\n            if !e.is_file {\n                continue;\n            }\n            if let Some((version, is_base)) = format::parse_versioned_name(&e.name) {\n                let data = format::read_whole(&vfs, &root.join(&e.name))?;\n                let _seg: Segment = format::decode_file(&e.name, &data)?;\n                if is_base {\n                    newest_base = newest_base.max(version);\n                }\n                on_disk.insert(\n                    version,\n                    FileMeta {\n                        is_base,\n                        size: data.len() as u64,\n                        stale: false,\n                    },\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Interrupted GC may have left files the new base obsoletes.\n        for (&v, meta) in &on_disk {\n            if v <= newest_base && !(meta.is_base && v == newest_base) {\n                let name = if meta.is_base {\n                    format::base_name(v)\n                } else {\n                    format::segment_name(v)\n                };\n                let _ = vfs.remove_file(&root.join(name));\n            }\n        }\n        on_disk.retain(|v, m| *v > newest_base || (m.is_base && *v == newest_base));\n\n        // Replay: base first, then surviving segments in version order.\n        let mut index: BTreeMap<Vec<u8>, Vec<Entry>> = BTreeMap::new();\n        let mut next_version = 1u64;\n        for (&v, meta) in &on_disk {\n            next_version = next_version.max(v + 1);\n            let name = if meta.is_base {\n                format::base_name(v)\n            } else {\n                format::segment_name(v)\n            };\n            let data = format::read_whole(&vfs, &root.join(&name))?;\n            let seg = format::decode_file(&name, &data)?;\n c.val,\n                    },\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(Engine {\n            inner: Arc::new(Mutex::new(Inner {\n                root,\n                vfs,\n on_disk,\n                next_tx_id: 1,\n                next_snap_id: 1,\n            })),\n            faults,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Fault-injection handle (no-op unless faults are armed).\n    pub fn faults(&self) -> &FaultVfs {\n        &self.faults\n    }\n\n    /// Begin a transaction; returns `(tx_id, read_version)`.\n    pub fn begin(&self) -> (u64, u64) {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let id = g.next_tx_id;\n        g.next_tx_id += 1;\n        let read_version = g.next_version - 1;\n        g.txs.insert(\n            id,\n            TxState {\n                read_version,\n                writes: BTreeMap::new(),\n            },\n        );\n        (id, read_version)\n    }\n\n    /// Pin an explicit long-lived read snapshot at the current version.\n    pub fn snapshot(&self) -> SnapshotInfo {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let id = g.next_snap_id;\n        g.next_snap_id += 1;\n        let info = SnapshotInfo {\n            id,\n            version: g.next_version - 1,\n        };\n        g.snapshots.insert(id, info.clone());\n        info\n    }\n\n    pub fn release_snapshot(&self, id: u64) -> Result<()> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        match g.snapshots.remove(&id) {\n            Some(_) => Ok(()),\n            None => Err(Error::UnknownSnapshot(id)),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn put(&self, tx: u64, key: Vec<u8>, val: Vec<u8>) -> Result<()> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        g.tx_mut(tx)?.writes.insert(key, Some(val));\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub fn delete(&self, tx: u64, key: Vec<u8>) -> Result<()> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        g.tx_mut(tx)?.writes.insert(key, None);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Read inside a transaction: own buffered writes win, otherwise the\n    /// newest committed version `<=` its read snapshot.\n    pub fn get_tx(&self, tx: u64, key: &[u8]) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>> {\n        let g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let t = g.txs.get(&tx).ok_or(Error::UnknownTx(tx))?;\n        if let Some(v) = t.writes.get(key) {\n            return Ok(v.clone());\n        }\n        Ok(read_at(&g.index, key, t.read_version))\n    }\n\n    /// Read through an explicit snapshot pin.\n    pub fn get_snapshot(&self, snap: u64, key: &[u8]) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>> {\n        let g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let s = g.snapshots.get(&snap).ok_or(Error::UnknownSnapshot(snap))?;\n        Ok(read_at(&g.index, key, s.version))\n    }\n\n    /// Abort/discard a transaction.\n    pub fn abort(&self, tx: u64) -> Result<()> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        match g.txs.remove(&tx) {\n            Some(_) => Ok(()),\n            None => Err(Error::UnknownTx(tx)),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Commit: first-writer-wins conflict check, then durable publication\n    /// at the next monotonic version.\n    ///\n    /// On I/O failure nothing is published and the transaction stays open\n    /// (the caller may retry the commit or abort).\n    pub fn commit(&self, tx: u64) -> Result<u64> {\n        // Phase 1: conflict check under the lock and stage the payload.\n        let (version, mut cells, file_size_hint) = {\n            let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n            let t = g.txs.get(&tx).ok_or(Error::UnknownTx(tx))?;\n            let read_version = t.read_version;\n            for key in t.writes.keys() {\n                if let Some(entry) = g.index.get(key).and_then(|v| v.last()) {\n                    if entry.version > read_version {\n                        return Err(Error::Conflict(key.clone()));\n                    }\n &mut cells);\n            (version, cells, body.len() as u64)\n        };\n\n        // Phase 2: durable publication (temp -> fsync -> rename -> fsync dir).\n        let name = format::segment_name(version);\n        let path = self.inner.lock().unwrap().root.join(name);\n        let body = {\n            let g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n            let mut cells2: };\n        // Publish through the VFS. Any error leaves no file behind.\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().vfs.write_atomic(&path, &body)?;\n\n        // Phase 3: publish into the in-memory index atomically with version.\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        // Another commit on the same engine cannot race (mutex), but defend\n        // the invariant explicitly.\n        assert_eq!(g.next_version, version, \"version allocated out of order\");\n        for c in cells.drain(..) {\n            apply_cell(\n                &mut g.index,\n                Entry {\n                    version,\n                    val: c.val,\n                },\n            );\n        }\n        g.files.insert(\n            version,\n            FileMeta {\n                is_base: false,\n                size: file_size_hint,\n                stale: false,\n            },\n        );\n        g.next_version = version + 1;\n        g.txs.remove(&tx);\n        Ok(version)\n    }\n\n    /// Current committed version.\n    pub fn current_version(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().next_version - 1\n    }\n\n    /// Snapshot pins, oldest first.\n    pub fn list_snapshots(&self) -> Vec<SnapshotInfo> {\n        let g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        g.snapshots.values().cloned().collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Compaction horizon: min read version over all active txs/snapshots.\n    fn horizon(g: &Inner) -> u64 {\n        let latest = g.next_version - 1;\n        let mut h = latest;\n        for t in g.txs.values() {\n            h = h.min(t.read_version);\n        }\n        for s in g.snapshots.values() {\n            h = h.min(s.version);\n        }\n        h\n    }\n\n    /// Run one reclamation pass. Minimal JSON value, parser and serializer — just enough for this\n//! project's HTTP requests and responses. Not a general-purpose JSON\n//! library (numbers are f64 on parse; the server emits integers itself).\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub enum Json {\n    Null,\n    Bool(bool),\n    Num(f64),\n    Str(String),\n    Arr(Vec<Json>),\n    Obj(BTreeMap<String, Json>),\n}\n\nimpl Json {\n    pub fn obj() -> Json {\n        Json::Obj(BTreeMap::new())\n    }\n\n    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&Json> {\n        match self {\n            Json::Obj(m) => m.get(key),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> Option<&str> {\n        match self {\n            Json::Str(s) => Some(s),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn as_u64(&self) -> Option<u64> {\n        match self {\n            Json::Num(n) if n.fract() == 0.0 => Some(*n as u64),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn as_bool(&self) -> Option<bool> {\n        match self {\n            Json::Bool(b) => Some(*b),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn as_array(&self) -> Option<&Vec<Json>> {\n        match self {\n            Json::Arr(a) => Some(a),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn insert(&mut self, key: &str, val: Json) {\n        if let Json::Obj(m) = self {\n            m.insert(key.to_string(), val);\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn string(val: impl Into<String>) -> Json {\n        Json::Str(val.into())\n    }\n\n    pub fn uint(val: u64) -> Json {\n        Json::Num(val as f64)\n    }\n\n    pub fn parse(input: &str) -> Result<Json, String> {\n        let bytes = input.as_bytes();\n        let mut pos = 0;\n        let v = Parser { bytes, pos: &mut pos }.parse_value()?;\n        skip_ws(bytes, &mut pos);\n        if pos != bytes.len() {\n            return Err(format!(\"trailing data at byte {pos}\"));\n        }\n        Ok(v)\n    }\n\n    /// Serialize compactly.\n    pub fn to_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8> {\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        self.write(&mut out);\n        out\n    }\n\n    fn write(&self, out: &mut Vec<u8>) {\n        match self {\n            Json::Null => out.extend_from_slice(b\"null\"),\n            Json::Bool(b) => out.extend_from_slice(if *b { b\"true\" } else { b\"false\" }),\n            Json::Num(n) => {\n                if n.fract() == 0.0 && n.is_finite() {\n                    out.extend_from_slice(format!(\"{}\", *n as i64).as_bytes());\n                } else {\n                    out.extend_from_slice(n.to_string().as_bytes());\n                }\n            }\n            Json::Str(s) => write_json_string(s, out),\n            Json::Arr(a) => {\n                out.push(b'[');\n                for (i, v) in a.iter().enumerate() {\n                    if i > 0 {\n                        out.push(b',');\n                    }\n                    v.write(out);\n                }\n                out.push(b']');\n            }\n            Json::Obj(m) => {\n                out.push(b'{');\n                for (i, (k, v)) in m.iter().enumerate() {\n                    if i > 0 {\n                        out.push(b',');\n                    }\n                    write_json_string(k, out);\n                    out.push(b':');\n                    v.write(out);\n                }\n                out.push(b'}');\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn write_json_string(s: &str, out: &mut Vec<u8>) {\n    out.push(b'\"');\n    for c in s.chars() {\n        match c {\n            '\"' => out.extend_from_slice(b\"\\\\\\\"\"),\n            '\\\\' => out.extend_from_slice(b\"\\\\\\\\\"),\n            '\\n' => out.extend_from_slice(b\"\\\\n\"),\n            '\\r' => out.extend_from_slice(b\"\\\\r\"),\n            '\\t' => out.extend_from_slice(b\"\\\\t\"),\n            c if (c as u32) < 0x20 => {\n                out.extend_from_slice(format!(\"\\\\u{:04x}\", c as u32).as_bytes())\n            }\n            c => {\n                let mut buf = [0u8; 4];\n                out.extend_from_slice(c.encode_utf8(&mut buf).as_bytes());\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    out.push(b'\"');\n}\n\nstruct Parser<'a> {\n    bytes: &'a [u8],\n    pos: &'a mut usize,\n}\n\nfn skip_ws(b: &[u8], pos: &mut usize) {\n    while *pos < b.len() && matches!(b[*pos], b' ' | b'\\t' | b'\\n' | b'\\r') {\n        *pos += 1;\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<'a> Parser<'a> {\n    fn parse_value(&mut self) -> Result<Json, String> {\n        skip_ws(self.bytes, self.pos);\n        if *self.pos >= self.bytes.len() {\n            return Err(\"unexpected end of input\".into());\n        }\n        match self.bytes[*self.pos] {\n            b'{' => self.parse_object(),\n            b'[' => self.parse_array(),\n            b'\"' => Ok(Json::Str(self.parse_string()?)),\n            b't' | b'f' => self.parse_bool(),\n            b'n' => self.parse_null(),\n            b'-' | b'0'..=b'9' => self.parse_number(),\n            c => Err(format!(\"unexpected byte {c} at {}\", self.pos)),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn parse_object(&mut self) -> Result<Json, String> {\n        *self.pos += 1; // {\n        let mut m = BTreeMap::new();\n        skip_ws(self.bytes, self.pos);\n        if self.peek() == Some(b'}') {\n            *self.pos += 1;\n            return Ok(Json::Obj(m));\n        }\n        loop {\n            skip_ws(self.bytes, self.pos);\n            let key = self.parse_string()?;\n            skip_ws(self.bytes, self.pos);\n            self.expect(b':')?;\n            let val = self.parse_value()?;\n            m.insert(key, val);\n            skip_ws(self.bytes, self.pos);\n            match self.next_byte() {\n                Some(b',') => continue,\n                Some(b'}') => break,\n                other => return Err(format!(\"expected , or }} got {other:?}\")),\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(Json::Obj(m))\n    }\n\n    fn parse_array(&mut self) -> Result<Json, String> {\n        *self.pos += 1; // [\n        let mut a = Vec::new();\n        skip_ws(self.bytes, self.pos);\n        if self.peek() == Some(b']') {\n            *self.pos += 1;\n            return Ok(Json::Arr(a));\n        }\n        loop {\n            a.push(self.parse_value()?);\n            skip_ws(self.bytes, self.pos);\n            match self.next_byte() {\n                Some(b',') => continue,\n                Some(b']') => break,\n                other => return Err(format!(\"expected , or ] got {other:?}\")),\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(Json::Arr(a))\n    }\n\n    fn parse_string(&mut self) -> Result<String, String> {\n        self.expect(b'\"')?;\n        let mut out = String::new();\n        loop {\n            match self.next_byte() {\n                None => return Err(\"unterminated string\".into()),\n                Some(b'\"') => break,\n                Some(b'\\\\') => match self.next_byte() {\n                    Some(b'\"') => out.push('\"'),\n                    Some(b'\\\\') => out.push('\\\\'),\n                    Some(b'/') => out.push('/'),\n                    Some(b'n') => out.push('\\n'),\n                    Some(b'r') => out.push('\\r'),\n                    Some(b't') => out.push('\\t'),\n                    Some(b'b') => out.push('\\u{0008}'),\n                    Some(b'f') => out.push('\\u{000C}'),\n                    Some(b'u') => {\n                        let cp = self.parse_hex4()?;\n                        if (0xD800..=0xDBFF).contains(&cp) {\n                            if self.next_byte() != Some(b'\\\\') || self.next_byte() != Some(b'u') {\n                                return Err(\"bad surrogate pair\".into());\n                            }\n                            let lo = self.parse_hex4()?;\n                            let c = 0x10000\n                                + (((cp - 0xD800) << 10) | (lo - 0xDC00));\n                            out.push(char::from_u32(c).ok_or(\"bad codepoint\")?);\n                        } else {\n                            out.push(char::from_u32(cp).ok_or(\"bad codepoint\")?);\n                        }\n                    }\n                    other => return Err(format!(\"bad escape {other:?}\")),\n                },\n                Some(b) => {\n                    // UTF-8 pass-through: collect the whole char.\n                    let width = utf8_width(b);\n                    let mut buf = vec![b];\n                    for _ in 1..width {\n out.push(char::from_u32(c).ok_or(\"bad codepoint\")?);\n                        } else {\n                            out.push(char::from_u32(cp).ok_or(\"bad codepoint\")?);\n                        }\n                    }\n                    other => return Err(format!(\"bad escape {other:?}\")),\n                },\n                Some(b) => {\n                    // UTF-8 pass-through: collect the whole char.\n                    let width = utf8_width(b);\n                    let mut buf = vec![b];\n                    for _ in 1..width {\n                        buf.push(self.next_byte().ok_or(\"bad utf-8 in string\")?);\n                    }\n                    out.push_str(std::str::from_utf8(&buf).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(out)\n    }\n\n    fn parse_hex4(&mut self) -> Result<u32, String> {\n        let mut v = 0u32;\n        for _ in 0..4 {\n            let b = self.next_byte().ok_or(\"short \\\\u escape\")?;\n            let d = match b {\n                b'0'..=b'9' => b - b'0',\n                b'a'..=b'f' => b - b'a' + 10,\n                b'A'..=b'F' => b - b'A' + 10,\n                _ => return Err(\"bad hex digit\".into()),\n            };\n            v = v * 16 + d as u32;\n        }\n        Ok(v)\n    }\n\n    fn parse_bool(&mut self) -> Result<Json, String> {\n        if self.bytes[*self.pos..].starts_with(b\"true\") {\n            *self.pos += 4;\n            Ok(Json::Bool(true))\n        } else if self.bytes[*self.pos..].starts_with(b\"false\") {\n            *self.pos += 5;\n            Ok(Json::Bool(false))\n        } else {\n            Err(\"bad literal\".into())\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn parse_null(&mut self) -> Result<Json, String> {\n        if self.bytes[*self.pos..].starts_with(b\"null\") {\n            *self.pos += 4;\n            Ok(Json::Null)\n        } else {\n            Err(\"bad literal\".into())\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn parse_number(&mut self) -> Result<Json, String> {\n        let start = *self.pos;\n        if self.peek() == Some(b'-') {\n            *self.pos += 1;\n        }\n        while let Some(b) = self.peek() {\n            if matches!(b, b'0'..=b'9' | b'.' | b'e' | b'E' | b'+' | b'-') {\n                *self.pos += 1;\n            } else {\n e.to_string())\n    }\n\n    fn expect(&mut self, b: u8) -> Result<(), String> {\n        if self.next_byte() == Some(b) {\n            Ok(())\n        } else {\n            Err(format!(\"expected byte {b} at {}\", *self.pos - 1))\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn peek(&self) -> Option<u8> {\n        self.bytes.get(*self.pos).copied()\n    }\n\n    fn next_byte(&mut self) -> Option<u8> {\n        let b = self.bytes.get(*self.pos).copied();\n        if b.is_some() {\n            *self.pos += 1;\n        }\n        b\n    }\n}\n\nfn utf8_width(first: u8) -> usize {\n    if first < 0x80 {\n        1\n    } else if first >> 5 == 0b110 {\n        2\n    } else if first >> 4 == 0b1110 {\n        3\n    } else if first >> 3 == 0b11110 {\n        4\n    } else {\n        1\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"f708a426-0445-4c74-a8c3-a7cb907896e5","session_id":"bafaec4f-110e-4e73-a9fd-df7bbf164629","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp3/b","sessionId":"bafaec4f-110e-4e73-a9fd-df7bbf164629","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp3-b","slug":"zany-questing-honey"}

{"parentUuid":"5f5d067c-c749-45bc-9b90-697430f57372","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_5a006ad6ec0e4f0aa799cffa","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp3/b/src/server.rs","content":"//! Minimal HTTP/1.1 server over `std::net` (no dependencies).\n//!\n//! One thread per connection, `Connection: close`, JSON in/out. All engine\n//! calls are made through the shared [`Engine`] handle; the engine's own\n//! mutex serializes state transitions, so this server is safe to hammer\n//! from concurrent clients.\n//!\n//! Endpoints (all JSON):\n//!\n//! | Method & path              | Body                        | Meaning |\n//! |----------------------------|-----------------------------|---------|\n//! | GET  /health               | —                           | liveness |\n//! | GET  /stats                | —                           | engine counters |\n//! | POST /tx/begin             | —                           | begin tx |\n//! | POST /tx/{id}/put          | {\"key\":\"k\",\"value\":\"v\"}     | buffer write |\n//! | POST /tx/{id}/delete       | {\"key\":\"k\"}                 | buffer delete |\n//! | POST /tx/{id}/get          | {\"key\":\"k\"}                 | read in tx |\n//! | POST /tx/{id}/commit       | —                           | commit (409 on conflict) |\n//! | POST /tx/{id}/abort        | —                           | abort |\n//! | POST /snapshot             | —                           | pin a snapshot |\n//! | POST /snapshot/{id}/get    | {\"key\":\"k\"}                 | read pinned snapshot |\n//! | POST /snapshot/{id}/release| —                           | release pin |\n//! | POST /gc                   | —                           | run reclamation |\n//! | GET  /admin/faults         | —                           | armed fault |\n//! | POST /admin/faults         | {\"op\":\"sync\",\"leave_written\":false} | arm one-shot fault |\n//! | POST /admin/faults/reset   | —                           | disarm |\n\nuse std::io::{self, Read, Write};\nuse std::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream};\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::thread;\n\nuse crate::engine::{Engine, GcReport, Stats};\nuse crate::error::Error;\nuse crate::json::Json;\nuse crate::vfs::FaultOp;\n\npub struct Server {\n    engine: Engine,\n    addr: String,\n}\n\nimpl Server {\n    pub fn new(engine: Engine, addr: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        Server {\n            engine,\n            addr: addr.into(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Bind and serve forever (blocking).\n    pub fn serve(self) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let listener = TcpListener::bind(&self.addr)?;\n        let engine = Arc::new(self.engine);\n        eprintln!(\"mvcc-gc listening on http://{}\", listener.local_addr()?);\n        for stream in listener.incoming() {\n            match stream {\n                Ok(s) => {\n                    let engine = engine.clone();\n                    thread::spawn(move || {\n                        let _ = handle_conn(s, engine);\n                    });\n                }\n                Err(e) => eprintln!(\"accept error: {e}\"),\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Route one request. Exposed for tests.\n    pub fn handle(&self, method: &str, path: &str, body: &[u8]) -> (u16, Json) {\n        route(&self.engine, method, path, body)\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Routing\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nfn route(engine: &Engine, method: &str, path: &str, body: &[u8]) -> (u16, Json) {\n    let result: crate::error::Result<Json> = (|| {\n        match (method, path) {\n            (\"GET\", \"/health\") => Ok(obj_with(\"status\", Json::string(\"ok\"))),\n            (\"GET\", \"/stats\") => Ok(stats_json(&engine.stats())),\n            (\"POST\", \"/tx/begin\") => {\n                let (id, read_version) = engine.begin();\n                let mut o = Json::obj();\n                o.insert(\"tx\", Json::uint(id));\n                o.insert(\"read_version\", Json::uint(read_version));\n                Ok(o)\n            }\n            (\"POST\", \"/snapshot\") => {\n                let s = engine.snapshot();\n                let mut o = Json::obj();\n                o.insert(\"snapshot\", Json::uint(s.id));\n                o.insert(\"version\", Json::uint(s.version));\n                Ok(o)\n            }\n            (\"POST\", \"/gc\") => Ok(gc_json(engine.gc()?)),\n            (\"GET\", \"/admin/faults\") => {\n                let mut o = Json::obj();\n                match engine.faults().armed() {\n                    Some(op) => o.insert(\"armed\", Json::string(op.as_str())),\n                    None => o.insert(\"armed\", Json::Null),\n                }\n                Ok(o)\n            }\n            (\"POST\", \"/admin/faults\") => {\n                let j = parse_body(body)?;\n                let op = j\n                    .get(\"op\")\n                    .and_then(Json::as_str)\n                    .and_then(FaultOp::parse)\n                    .ok_or_else(|| {\n                        Error::BadRequest(\n                            \"op must be one of write|sync|rename|sync_parent|remove\".into(),\n                        )\n                    })?;\n                let leave = j.get(\"leave_written\").and_then(Json::as_bool).unwrap_or(false);\n                engine.faults().arm(op, leave);\n                let mut o = Json::obj();\n                o.insert(\"armed\", Json::string(op.as_str()));\n                o.insert(\"leave_written\", Json::Bool(leave));\n                Ok(o)\n            }\n            (\"POST\", \"/admin/faults/reset\") => {\n                engine.faults().disarm();\n                Ok(obj_with(\"disarmed\", Json::Bool(true)))\n            }\n            _ => route_dynamic(engine, method, path, body),\n        }\n    })();\n\n    match result {\n        Ok(mut j) => {\n            j.insert(\"ok\", Json::Bool(true));\n            (200, j)\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            let status = match &e {\n                Error::NotFound | Error::UnknownTx(_) | Error::UnknownSnapshot(_) => 404,\n                Error::Conflict(_) => 409,\n                Error::BadRequest(_) => 400,\n                _ => 500,\n            };\n            let mut j = Json::obj();\n            j.insert(\"ok\", Json::Bool(false));\n            j.insert(\"error\", Json::string(e.to_string()));\n            (status, j)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn route_dynamic(\n    engine: &Engine,\n    method: &str,\n    path: &str,\n    body: &[u8],\n) -> crate::error::Result<Json> {\n    // /tx/{id}/{action}\n    if let Some(rest) = path.strip_prefix(\"/tx/\") {\n        let (id, action) = split_id(rest)?;\n        match (method, action) {\n            (\"POST\", \"put\") => {\n                let j = parse_body(body)?;\n                let key = body_key(&j)?;\n                let value = j\n                    .get(\"value\")\n                    .and_then(Json::as_str)\n                    .ok_or_else(|| Error::BadRequest(\"missing string field \\\"value\\\"\".into()))?;\n                engine.put(id, key.into_bytes(), value.as_bytes().to_vec())?;\n                return Ok(obj_with(\"buffered\", Json::Bool(true)));\n            }\n            (\"POST\", \"delete\") => {\n                let j = parse_body(body)?;\n                engine.delete(id, body_key(&j)?.into_bytes())?;\n                return Ok(obj_with(\"buffered\", Json::Bool(true)));\n            }\n            (\"POST\", \"get\") => {\n                let j = parse_body(body)?;\n                let key = body_key(&j)?;\n                return Ok(value_json(engine.get_tx(id, key.as_bytes())?, key));\n            }\n            (\"POST\", \"commit\") => {\n                let version = engine.commit(id)?;\n                return Ok(obj_with(\"version\", Json::uint(version)));\n            }\n            (\"POST\", \"abort\") => {\n                engine.abort(id)?;\n                return Ok(obj_with(\"aborted\", Json::Bool(true)));\n            }\n            _ => {}\n        }\n    }\n\n    // /snapshot/{id}/{action}\n    if let Some(rest) = path.strip_prefix(\"/snapshot/\") {\n        let (id, action) = split_id(rest)?;\n        match (method, action) {\n            (\"POST\", \"get\") => {\n                let j = parse_body(body)?;\n                let key = body_key(&j)?;\n                return Ok(value_json(engine.get_snapshot(id, key.as_bytes())?, key));\n            }\n            (\"POST\", \"release\") => {\n                engine.release_snapshot(id)?;\n                return Ok(obj_with(\"released\", Json::Bool(true)));\n            }\n            _ => {}\n        }\n    }\n\n    Err(Error::BadRequest(format!(\"no route for {method} {path}\")))\n}\n\nfn split_id(rest: &str) -> crate::error::Result<(u64, &str)> {\n    let (id_s, action) = rest\n        .split_once('/')\n        .ok_or_else(|| Error::BadRequest(\"expected /{id}/{action}\".into()))?;\n    let id: u64 = id_s\n        .parse()\n        .map_err(|_| Error::BadRequest(format!(\"bad id {id_s:?}\")))?;\n    Ok((id, action))\n}\n\nfn parse_body(body: &[u8]) -> crate::error::Result<Json> {\n    if body.is_empty() {\n        return Ok(Json::obj());\n    }\n    let s = std::str::from_utf8(body)\n        .map_err(|_| Error::BadRequest(\"body is not utf-8\".into()))?;\n    Json::parse(s).map_err(Error::BadRequest)\n}\n\nfn body_key(j: &Json) -> crate::error::Result<&str> {\n    j.get(\"key\")\n        .and_then(Json::as_str)\n        .ok_or_else(|| Error::BadRequest(\"missing string field \\\"key\\\"\".into()))\n}\n\nfn value_json(found: Option<Vec<u8>>, key: &str) -> Json {\n    let mut o = Json::obj();\n    o.insert(\"key\", Json::string(key));\n    match found {\n        Some(v) => {\n            o.insert(\"found\", Json::Bool(true));\n            o.insert(\n                \"value\",\n                Json::string(String::from_utf8_lossy(&v).into_owned()),\n            );\n        }\n        None => {\n            o.insert(\"found\", Json::Bool(false));\n        }\n    }\n    o\n}\n\nfn obj_with(k: &str, v: Json) -> Json {\n    let mut o = Json::obj();\n    o.insert(k, v);\n    o\n}\n\nfn stats_json(s: &Stats) -> Json {\n    let mut o = Json::obj();\n    o.insert(\"current_version\", Json::uint(s.current_version));\n    o.insert(\"base_version\", Json::uint(s.base_version));\n    o.insert(\"keys\", Json::uint(s.keys as u64));\n    o.insert(\"live_cells\", Json::uint(s.live_cells as u64));\n    o.insert(\n        \"open_transactions\",\n        Json::Arr(\n            s.open_transactions\n                .iter()\n                .map(|(id, rv)| {\n                    let mut t = Json::obj();\n                    t.insert(\"tx\", Json::uint(*id));\n                    t.insert(\"read_version\", Json::uint(*rv));\n                    t\n                })\n                .collect(),\n        ),\n    );\n    o.insert(\n        \"snapshots\",\n        Json::Arr(\n            s.snapshots\n                .iter()\n                .map(|s| {\n                    let mut t = Json::obj();\n                    t.insert(\"snapshot\", Json::uint(s.id));\n                    t.insert(\"version\", Json::uint(s.version));\n                    t\n                })\n                .collect(),\n        ),\n    );\n    let mut files = Json::obj();\n    files.insert(\"segments\", Json::uint(s.segment_files as u64));\n    files.insert(\"bases\", Json::uint(s.base_files as u64));\n    files.insert(\"stale\", Json::uint(s.stale_files as u64));\n    files.insert(\"live_bytes\", Json::uint(s.live_bytes));\n    files.insert(\"stale_bytes\", Json::uint(s.stale_bytes));\n    o.insert(\"files\", files);\n    o\n}\n\nfn gc_json(r: GcReport) -> Json {\n    let mut o = Json::obj();\n    o.insert(\"horizon\", Json::uint(r.horizon));\n    o.insert(\"base_version_before\", Json::uint(r.base_version_before));\n    o.insert(\"base_written\", Json::Bool(r.base_written));\n    o.insert(\"base_cells\", Json::uint(r.base_cells as u64));\n    o.insert(\"files_removed\", Json::uint(r.files_removed as u64));\n    o.insert(\"bytes_reclaimed\", Json::uint(r.bytes_reclaimed));\n    o.insert(\"stale_left\", Json::uint(r.stale_left as u64));\n    match r.noop_reason {\n        Some(reason) => o.insert(\"noop_reason\", Json::string(reason)),\n        None => o.insert(\"noop_reason\", Json::Null),\n    }\n    o\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// HTTP wire\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nconst MAX_HEAD: usize = 64 * 1024;\nconst MAX_BODY: usize = 16 * 1024 * 1024;\n\nfn handle_conn(mut stream: TcpStream, engine: Arc<Engine>) -> io::Result<()> {\n    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(4096);\n    let mut chunk = [0u8; 8192];\n\n    // Read headers.\n    let head_end = loop {\n        if let Some(pos) = find_subslice(&buf, b\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\") {\n            break pos + 4;\n        }\n        let n = stream.read(&mut chunk)?;\n        if n == 0 {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..n]);\n        if buf.len() > MAX_HEAD {\n            return write_response(&mut stream, 431, b\"{\\\"ok\\\":false,\\\"error\\\":\\\"head too large\\\"}\");\n        }\n    };\n\n    let head = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf[..head_end]).into_owned();\n    let mut lines = head.split(\"\\r\\n\");\n    let request_line = lines.next().unwrap_or_default();\n    let mut parts = request_line.split_whitespace();\n    let method = parts.next().unwrap_or(\"\").to_string();\n    let path = parts.next().unwrap_or(\"\").to_string();\n\n    let mut content_length = 0usize;\n    for line in lines {\n        if let Some((name, value)) = line.split_once(':') {\n            if name.trim().eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"content-length\") {\n                content_length = value.trim().parse().unwrap_or(0);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    if content_length > MAX_BODY {\n        return write_response(&mut stream, 413, b\"{\\\"ok\\\":false,\\\"error\\\":\\\"body too large\\\"}\");\n    }\n\n    // Read the rest of the body.\n    let mut body = buf.split_off(head_end);\n    while body.len() < content_length {\n        let n = stream.read(&mut chunk)?;\n        if n == 0 {\n            break;\n        }\n        body.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..n]);\n    }\n    body.truncate(content_length);\n\n    let server = Server {\n        engine: (*engine).clone(),\n        addr: String::new(),\n    };\n    let (status, json) = server.handle(&method, &path, &body);\n    let payload = json.to_bytes();\n    write_response(&mut stream, status, &payload)\n}\n\nfn write_response(stream: &mut TcpStream, status: u16, payload: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()> {\n    let reason = match status {\n        200 => \"OK\",\n        400 => \"Bad Request\",\n        404 => \"Not Found\",\n        409 => \"Conflict\",\n        413 => \"Payload Too Large\",\n        431 => \"Request Header Fields Too Large\",\n        _ => \"Internal Server Error\",\n    };\n    let head = format!(\n        \"HTTP/1.1 {status} {reason}\\r\\ncontent-type: application/json\\r\\ncontent-length: {}\\r\\nconnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n\",\n        payload.len()\n    );\n    stream.write_all(head.as_bytes())?;\n    stream.write_all(payload)?;\n    stream.flush()\n}\n\nfn find_subslice(haystack: &[u8], needle: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {\n    haystack\n        .windows(needle.len())\n        .position(|w| w ==
